utterances.text: Yes, then perhaps we should wait until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would already would ask Mr. Konings but already to leave us, but I would first like to give you the same instruction as I gave you before, that is that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony. And we would like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to inquire with the parties about timing. Mr. Kehoe, I think tomorrow after the first session you will be done with your three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Absolutely. I will be done well before that, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kuzmanovic, I am informed that you might need approximately one session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, probably less, but I will take the full session if I need it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, same as far as the Cermak defence is concerned. Mr. Russo, could you give us an estimate as matters stand now how much time you will need for re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Approximately half an hour, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Approximately half an hour, which gives a fair expectation that we will not have to have Mr. Konings to come back on Thursday and that he can finish his testimony tomorrow, perhaps even before the end of tomorrow's hearing. Mr. Russo, will that cause you problem in relation to your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe we had intended to call the next witness on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On Thursday, yes, which is then -- we'll see to what extent question deal with other procedural matters. Otherwise, we might have to delay that until Thursday. But I'll see to what extent I can prepare and have a full oversight on the list, but there are matter we can deal with tomorrow. Then finally, Mr. Kehoe, I was a bit lost in reference to your pages 7079, line 19, through page 7081, line 8. I am not fully aware what I am supposed to find there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I believe that during the cross-examination by Mr. Misetic of Mr. Roberts, Mr. Roberts said that there was a provisional assessment and a final assessment and that the final assessment was consistent with the provisional assessment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, what I found until now is that on the first line you mention that Mr. Misetic put Exhibit P228 to the witness and that a part of that was read to him, and that he mainly emphasised that reports that were put to him were certainly not the only ones. And there is one thing where he was asked whether this P228 suggests this or that and then he said, The document does not say so or suggest that, but there were more -- I did not find as a matter of fact, consistency between provisional assessment and final assessment. That's what I found and that is the reason why I'm asking you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can go back and take a look the transcript again, I will present it first think in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'd like to -- Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is it actually at page 7082. Actually it starts at 7081, line 13 and goes through 7082, line 6, and actually at lines 4 and 5 of page 7082 he says: "I think I recall seeing the final document that went up and that it concurred with their initial assessment." And then I will find you Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, you now draw my attention to another portion of the -- of course, you will understand that if Mr. Kehoe gives me a source that I'm not going through all of the -- not going through all of the -- how many are there at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, let me also say that by tomorrow morning I will get you -- I know Mr. Waespi did a re-direct examination on this point where the witness was even more explicitly clear on this point [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. I'm just inquiring, but if I get sources, then of course I'm not going through the 14.000 other pages but rather focus on the sources given to me. And as I said, I didn't say nothing more than I couldn't find it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My apologies, Mr. President, for the wrong page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will we adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 20th of January, 9.00 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.
